entries.effect: the shape of a texture, as a value: a channel format, a width, a height, a feature channel count, an image count and a usage, from which the pixel format is derived and a texture built. Copies compare by value and hash by the same fields, so two descriptors that name the same texture are equal. Measured by the five cases of tests/backports/host/mpscnn/run.sh, which build every source and destination through +imageDescriptorWithChannelFormat:width:height:featureChannels: and -initWithDevice:imageDescriptor: on the port's side; see the MPSImage row for the measurement.

the image is a real texture on the port's carried Metal classes, made through MTLTextureDescriptor and read and written through the texture's own getBytes: and replaceRegion:, which is the shape the release takes. Measured by tests/backports/host/mpscnn/run.sh on macOS 27.0 (build 26A428), which builds each of its six cases' source and destination through this class on the port's side and through the release's on its own: the four pooling cases and fresh-image are bit-identical and batch-normalization differs on one of nine elements, 0.00118 of the case's 1e-4 tolerance, which is the accumulation order and not a different answer. Two mutants say the comparison can fail: the average's divisor one short takes `differing cases: 0` to 3, and a fresh image filled with 0x7F7F7F7F instead of asked for as zeros takes it to 1. Before this class existed the port side's MPSImage resolved to the release's own and the five cases then compared the release with itself; tests/backports/host/mpscnn/cnn-cases.m now refuses a case whose classes the port does not have, and the run is red while that is so.
